data.name: Runeyana
data.detailed_description:
Runeyana is an RPG that combines Hack and Slash action. It evokes a story of bravery, strength, courage, trust and the desire to overcome destiny. Set in a deep, responsive, huge world, you will explore a beautiful sprawling land gaining the trust of various species scattered throughout the world. As in real life, you will cope with internal racial tensions by obtaining their trust through reputation. Use unique weapons and craft your character in both physical and psychological customisation.

Features


Role Playing Game mixing Hack and Slash action
Online trade and looting support
Leveling up
Learn your enemies’ abilities.
Storyline based on the ancient gods of Runeyana
Game goes through the bone age to the stone age
Questing and NPC system
Pet system too!
Create your own army
Buy your own buildings and hire guardians to protect yourself from players online. Become the King of Alteos by owning as many buildings as possible.

reviews.review:
Runeyana is an independent fantasy action RPG with an unusually broad collection of ideas, mixing hack-and-slash fighting with exploration, character progression, quests, reputation management, property ownership, pets, trading, and even army development. Developed and published by Blackturn Ltd, it aims for something larger than a straightforward dungeon crawler. The result is an ambitious but noticeably rough adventure whose appeal comes from the variety of systems it attempts to combine rather than exceptional refinement in any single area.

The world has a primitive fantasy character that helps distinguish it from the usual medieval RPG setting. Civilization is presented as developing from the bone age toward the stone age, while ancient gods, different species, social tensions, and questions of destiny provide the background for the player's journey. Themes involving courage, trust, strength, and relationships are incorporated into the adventure. There is an interesting foundation here, particularly for players who enjoy fantasy worlds that experiment with their own mythology instead of simply reproducing familiar knights-and-castles conventions.

Combat follows a direct hack-and-slash structure. Fighting enemies, collecting loot, acquiring weapons, and improving the character form an important part of the gameplay loop. One of the more distinctive concepts is the ability to obtain abilities associated with enemies, potentially making encounters valuable for more than experience and equipment. Character development also extends beyond ordinary physical progression, with the game presenting psychological development as part of its customization concept. These systems give the adventure a sense that the protagonist is supposed to evolve both as a fighter and as an individual within the world.

NPC relationships and reputation provide another layer of progression. Different species inhabit Runeyana, and gaining their trust can become an important part of advancing through the experience. Quests contribute to these relationships while giving players reasons to explore and interact with the inhabitants rather than treating everything outside combat as scenery. The concept is appealing because reputation can make actions feel connected to the wider society. The execution does not always have the sophistication found in larger RPGs, but the attempt to make social standing meaningful gives the game additional personality.

The scope expands further through pets, buildings, guardians, and armies. Players can acquire property and hire protection, while the larger ambition of becoming the King of Alteos gives wealth and ownership a purpose beyond simply accumulating resources. Building an army introduces a strategic flavor that contrasts with the personal scale of hack-and-slash encounters. These mechanics suggest a progression from relatively ordinary adventurer to someone possessing genuine influence and power. It is one of the more interesting parts of the overall concept, even though the individual systems can feel less developed than their descriptions initially suggest.

Trading and looting complement this progression by encouraging the acquisition and management of useful items. With weapons, abilities, property, allies, pets, and reputation all contributing to advancement, Runeyana constantly offers another system to investigate. This abundance is simultaneously one of its strengths and weaknesses. There is considerable variety for such a modest independent production, but spreading attention across so many features prevents some mechanics from reaching their full potential.

Presentation is functional rather than spectacular. The game's age and independent origins are apparent in its visuals, interface, animation, and general level of polish. Players accustomed to modern large-budget action RPGs may find the experience dated or awkward. On the positive side, the modest technical requirements make it suitable for less powerful computers. Its strongest qualities are therefore found in experimentation, progression, and the unusual collection of mechanics rather than graphical spectacle.

Steam Deck users should consider the game playable rather than assume a completely optimized handheld experience. Compatibility information indicates that it can run on Steam Deck, but it should not be treated as equivalent to an official Steam Deck Verified designation. Its relatively straightforward mechanics make handheld play feasible, although occasional adjustments or minor interface inconveniences may be possible. Players specifically buying or installing games for Deck use should therefore expect functional compatibility rather than guaranteed console-like optimization.

Runeyana ultimately feels like a game driven by ambition. It tries to offer combat, role-playing, relationships, exploration, reputation, character customization, pets, property, guardians, armies, trading, and a path toward becoming a ruler inside one fantasy adventure. That scope makes it intriguing, particularly for players who enjoy discovering obscure RPGs with unconventional mechanics. At the same time, its rough presentation and uneven depth prevent all those ideas from forming a consistently polished whole.

Players who value experimentation and can tolerate technical or design roughness may discover an interesting RPG curiosity here. Those expecting highly polished combat, elaborate storytelling, or deeply developed versions of every advertised mechanic are more likely to be disappointed. There are plenty of interesting ideas beneath the imperfections, but appreciating them requires accepting the limitations of a small and ambitious production.

Rating: 5/10
